baseline.notes: The designated AwesomeSalesforceSkills-main (3).zip archive was mounted and hashed. Its SHA-256 matches the earlier inspectable (1).zip fallback byte-for-byte, so reconciliation used commit 7e0ecaba888f3d986362782f04d7035064bfce34 created from the (3) extract as the exact latest baseline. Upstream candidate archives remain unavailable for byte-level pins.

pin.reason: The user-supplied archive was not mounted, so no archive hash, commit, or tag is asserted for the reviewed snapshot.

sources.content_use: Broad Apex/LWC skill and ruleset inventory was used only to challenge local gap coverage; no prose or ruleset text was copied.

decisions.target: existing apex, flow, integration, security, and devops packages
decisions.scope: Do not add a broad umbrella developer skill or duplicate Apex coding-rules corpus.
decisions.rationale: The canonical repository already owns these concerns through narrow packages, domain routers, runtime agents, templates, anti-patterns, and deterministic checkers; another umbrella would weaken routing.
decisions.routing: Use the existing domain router and narrow skill selected by task; use /build-apex, /review, /scan-security, or /gen-tests for runtime orchestration.

decisions.scope: Add a behavior-preserving, version-aware LWC JavaScript-to-TypeScript migration workflow.
decisions.rationale: The corpus covered LWC building, auditing, security, testing, and framework migrations but lacked one owner for native-versus-build TypeScript strategy, type debt, generated output ownership, and target validation.
decisions.routing: Use lwc/lwc-typescript-migration only for converting or auditing JavaScript-to-TypeScript migration; keep general component creation in existing LWC builder packages.

validation.command: new skill checker passing and failing fixtures

attestation.clean_room: The reported MIT license permits reuse, but the unavailable archive prevents pin-level verification. The integration therefore uses clean-room original content and official Salesforce sources only.
attestation.product_boundary: All accepted additions remain read-only analysis, teaching, retrieval, or local validation guidance. They do not deploy, mutate an org, grant authority, or bypass the V2.0/V2.1/V2.2 product gates.
